title: Pre-Push Orphan GC Quarantine (full mark-and-sweep)
desc: Pre-push harness guard that runs a FULL GC mark-and-sweep: roots = all .md docs + entry configs + tracked list; transitively mark file-to-file reference edges to a fixpoint; sweep unmarked files to .tmp/unused-DATE/; friendly notice; push always exits 0 (never blocks). Over-mark safety bias keeps runtime-referenced files alive.
steps: PURPOSE: a pre-push harness guard that auto-quarantines orphan (unreferenced) files so the repo stays clean WITHOUT blocking the push. Non-destructive, transparent, always exit 0.

MODEL is GC mark-and-sweep run FULLY each push. ROOTS = every .md doc PLUS entry configs (settings.json, csproj, sln, package.json, harness entry scripts) PLUS the tracked file list. Unmarked-after-mark = garbage.

MARK is TRANSITIVE: from each root follow file-to-file reference edges, then follow the references of THOSE files, to a fixpoint. The doc is only the root; a referenced source that references another source keeps that one alive too.

EDGE EXTRACTION is language-aware per extension: ps1 dot-source and Import-Module and -File; cs via csproj Compile Include and project membership; py import and from; sh source and dot; js and ts import and require; generic = any path-like string literal. Build a directed graph.

OVER-MARK SAFETY BIAS: when an edge is ambiguous TREAT IT AS AN EDGE and keep the file. A spurious edge means a file survives (safe); a missed edge means a false quarantine (recoverable but bad). Always fail toward KEEPING, never under-mark.
ALGORITHM: BFS or DFS from roots with a visited-set for cycle safety (A to B to A), iterate to fixpoint (no new marks added).
SWEEP: move each unmarked file to .tmp/unused-DATE/ preserving its relative path. MOVE not delete (recoverable). Never touch .git or anything already under .tmp.
RUNTIME-CRITICAL BACKSTOP: never quarantine known-config (.gitignore, csproj, sln, LICENSE, lock files); the entry-config roots plus transitive mark should already cover these.
NOTIFY then PASS: print a friendly stderr line listing each moved file plus destination plus how to recover from .tmp/unused-DATE/. The guard NEVER blocks: exit 0 always. It cleaned, it did not deny.

ROLLOUT: ship as dry-run LIST mode first (log candidates, move nothing) to calibrate edge extraction on real repos; promote to live-move only after the candidate list is verified accurate. Scope: AI-session pushes.

BUILD FLOW: haiku prototypes the mark-sweep plus edge extraction in a sandbox proto; sonnet architects and implements; ROOT verifies synthetic plus live plus static then merges. See haiku-sandbox-problem-solving and verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static.

SIMPLIFICATION (user 2026-06-19, recoverability lets the mark be approximate): full fixpoint is NOT required. Bound the transitive traversal to about 3 hops from roots -- because any false quarantine is recoverable from .tmp/unused-DATE/, exhaustive marking is over-engineering. Prefer the simpler bounded walk. EDGE FOCUS: primarily follow references that involve ROOT SCRIPTS (a file referencing a root script, plus that root script own references); do not chase every generic path string to infinity. NOTE: a root script referencing ANOTHER root script is a mild code-smell (not beautiful) -- tolerated, but flat cross-references among roots are a sign to flatten and clarify, not to deepen the walk.

ACTION POLICY (user 2026-06-19, TWO-TIER by location): an UNREFERENCED file at the REPO ROOT (top-level) is IMMEDIATELY QUARANTINED -- moved to .tmp/unused-DATE/ (the root must stay clean). An unreferenced file in a SUBFOLDER gets a WARN ONLY -- listed in the notice, NOT moved. WHY: root cruft is most visible and the root candidate set is small and controlled so auto-move is safe there; subfolder auto-move is risky because dynamic loaders cause false-positives (e.g. tools/ harness modules that static edge-extraction misses -- a real calibration run flagged 249/505 incl live harness), so warn-not-move avoids any brick. BOTH paths: push still exits 0, never blocks. Enumeration may recurse (to WARN on subfolders), but the MOVE action applies to TOP-LEVEL files only.

a ps1 dot-sourced by an md-referenced script but absent from every md
requirements.expect: NOT a candidate (kept via transitive mark)
